The LA County Heat Action Plan (CHAP) represents Los Angeles County’s first multisector plan solely focused on addressing the risks associated with rising temperatures and
extreme heat. Developed with input from hundreds of partners, the CHAP
provides a strategic coordination framework to unite County departments,
other local and regional government agencies, community organizations
and businesses to take action on both outdoor and indoor heat risks. The
CHAP is grounded in climate science, public health evidence, and the lived
experiences of residents most affected by extreme heat. It is intended to
guide and align policy, planning, and investment decisions that reduce heat
exposure and improve resilience.

title: National Climate Change and Health Policy and Revised Action Plan - Marshall Islands
organization: Ministry of Health and Human Services, Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (MOHHS)
landscapes: Small Island Developing States, Tropical and Subtropical, Household, Institutional, Occupational, Athletics
description: This national climate change and health policy and revised action plan sets out priorities and actions to strengthen climate-resilient health systems in the Marshall Islands. It addresses climate-sensitive health risks including food and water safety, vector-borne diseases, non-communicable diseases, mental health and psychosocial well-being, respiratory diseases, and extreme weather events. The plan also includes heat-related preparedness strategies such as community heat education, rest and hydration guidance, shifting outdoor activities to cooler times of day, and reducing overheating in homes.

organization: World Health Organization Centre for Health Development (WHO Kobe Centre) (WHO; WKC)
landscapes: Urban, Household, Institutional, Occupational, Athletics
description: This technical report supports Hyogo Prefecture, Japan in developing a comprehensive heat-health action framework to prevent and manage the public health effects of heat waves. It proposes objectives for heat-risk prediction, protection of vulnerable populations, intersectoral coordination and communication, and long-term urban planning, and outlines risk phases and possible interventions for implementation.
